applicant_utility.summary: The DAAD architecture scholarship pays EUR 992 a month for a German Master's or a non-degree complementary year, but it never pays tuition, so any fee-charging programme has to be financed out of the stipend. The 2027 round closed on 23 September 2026 with selection in January 2027 and funding from September 2027, so treat the 1 June portal opening as the practical start of your preparation window. What actually separates successful applicants is the portfolio: the committee scores architectural maturity from study achievements and work samples, not from the CV alone.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Architecture, interior design, urban design or landscape architecture graduates within roughly six years of their first degree who can name specific German Master's programmes and assemble a clean A4 portfolio of student design work.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify the ECTS credit-point split of every shortlisted German programme before applying - under 45 CP of Design/Projects in a 120 CP Master's rules the programme out entirely.
Build the portfolio to DAAD's architecture rules early: maximum 20 DIN A4 pages, maximum 50 MB, three to five drafts at an appropriate scale, one of them an independent non-group project.
Book a TestDaF or an IELTS/TOEFL sitting now and keep the certificate inside a three-year window at the deadline.
Check each host university's own admission deadline, which often falls months before the DAAD selection result.
Keep commercial office work out of the portfolio; only student projects, analyses and your own prize entries belong there.
common_rejection_risks: Work samples uploaded to the DAAD portal instead of the DAAD media database are invisible to the committee.
A Design/Projects credit-point shortfall in the chosen programme, caught at formal check and not negotiable.
Missing German or English translations of national-language transcripts and degree certificates.
Naming degree programmes in the motivation letter that are absent from the 'Information about your preferred master programmes' form - only the listed programmes count.
Having been resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline.
Applying for a Master's or postgraduate programme that has already started in Germany, which cannot be funded.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees at the host university, which DAAD explicitly does not pay (non-EU students at Baden-Württemberg state universities pay EUR 1,500 per semester and TUM charges EUR 4,000-6,000 per semester on some Master's programmes), semester contributions, university entrance examination costs, and rent above the EUR 992 stipend in expensive cities unless a rent subsidy of up to EUR 350 per month is granted.
document_audit: The portfolio must stay legible when printed on A4 - one draft per page, never several compiled together.
The signed authorship declaration is a separate DAAD form; a portfolio without it is incomplete.
The list of designs/plans needs size, date of creation and place for each item, not just titles.
Transcripts must carry an explanation of the grading system, since German committees cannot read foreign scales unaided.
alerts: The portal for this programme only appears while the application period runs - after the deadline you cannot even log in to fix a missing file.
The work-sample link arrives only after the formal check (by 23 October) and uploads close on 4 November CET; the application is not complete without that second step.
A DAAD scholarship does not guarantee a university place - if you are not admitted to any programme listed in your application, you cannot use the award already granted.
Funding for a study period abroad is limited to a quarter of the scholarship period (up to 50% for joint and double-degree programmes specified in the study regulations).
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register and submit the documents in the DAAD portal between 1 June and the deadline, then upload the work samples to the DAAD media database once the link arrives - both steps must land for the file to count.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a stipend rather than a fully funded package: EUR 992 a month plus insurance payments and a travel allowance, with tuition explicitly excluded, so a fee-charging programme would have to be financed out of the monthly payment. The window closes at midnight CET/CEST on 15 October 2026, with selection in April 2027 and funding from October 2027, making it one of the latest deadlines among the DAAD art programmes. Because a special committee of professors from German art, design and film schools judges the portfolio, presentation quality and the supplementary list matter as much as the work itself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent arts graduates within roughly six years of their first degree who already work in fine art, design, visual communication or film and can commit to a full-time, attendance-based German programme or a supervised complementary year.
application_readiness_checklist: Rebuild the portfolio to DAAD's exact format rules: one PDF of at most 30 pages and 50 MB for fine art, design and visual communication; up to 20 minutes of video material for film.
Name every file as DAAD reference number_Name_First name_Field of study_Name of work so it reaches the right specialist committee.
Fill in the supplementary list template and credit every collaborator's role in film and group works.
Obtain a language certificate for the language of instruction that is less than three years old at the deadline.
For a complementary year, secure the German professor's confirmation of supervision, or written proof of credit recognition from your home university, before submitting.
common_rejection_risks: Uploading the portfolio or still images to the DAAD portal - DAAD rejects them there and the application stays incomplete.
Submitting a showreel or trailer for film, or exceeding the 30-page or 20-minute caps, since material outside the limits is not accepted for review.
A motivation letter longer than three pages, or curriculum screenshots used as a substitute for the 'Information about your preferred master programmes' form.
Choosing a part-time, extra-occupational or mainly online programme, which is explicitly excluded.
An arts-adjacent field such as history of art, art studies or restoration, which belongs to a different DAAD programme.
Completing the portal step but letting the media-database upload lapse, which voids the application.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees at the host institution (DAAD does not pay them), semester contributions, rent above the EUR 992 stipend in high-rent cities unless a rent subsidy of up to EUR 350 per month is granted, travel costs beyond the country-specific flat travel allowance, and portfolio printing, formatting and translation costs.
document_audit: Portfolio, supplementary list and declaration must all reach the DAAD media database; the portal part alone is not enough.
Permitted formats are limited to MP3, WAV, MPEG, MP4, MOV, JPEG, JPG, PNG, TIF, GIF, PDF, INDD, PSD, CR2, EPS, DOC, DOCX, XML, PPTX and PPT - anything else is not reviewed.
Hyperlinks to video or audio must be reachable without creating a new account and must stay inside the page or time limits.
Supervision confirmation or credit-recognition proof is required only for complementary studies; a Master's applicant needs the study-programme form instead.
Language certificates older than three years at the deadline will not be accepted.
alerts: The application is only valid once both the DAAD portal and the DAAD media database hold all required documents - finish the second step, not just the first.
Up to seven months can pass between submission and the selection decision, so do not give up work or book flights on the assumption of an earlier answer.
A DAAD Scholarship Award Letter only becomes valid if you are admitted to the host university named in your application.

Funding for a Master's or postgraduate programme that has already started in Germany cannot be granted, and a study period abroad is limited to a quarter of the scholarship period (up to 50% for joint and double-degree programmes).
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in the DAAD portal, complete the online form and upload PDFs before 15 October 2026, then wait for the media-database link that follows the formal check and upload the portfolio plus supplementary list by the stated deadline.
